strings.YUN_THENEWORDER_DESC: In the aftermath of the collapse of the Chinese United Front, the former ruler of Yunnan handed the reins to Lu Han, who immediately began to go through the motions of modernizing it, whether by hook or by crook. But this came at a terrible cost. Corruption and societal ills have spread like the plague; dissension and misery have engulfed the country. Due to all this, the province, though experiencing an economic boom, is also becoming a hotbed of anti-Japanese sentiment. Lu Han goes on in blissful unawareness of the situation, continuing with Gao's plans for his region, but there are others in Kunming and elsewhere who might take advantage of the chaos behind the scenes to take Yunnan down a path no-one had expected...

strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1:
To look at the former province of Yunnan, nestled in the far southwest of China, one must first understand the aftermath of the defeat at Chongqing. The final victory of Japan in the Battle of Chongqing severely damaged the morale of the United Front forces in Yunnan. This combined with the fall of Southeast Asia under Japanese control, meant that there was no way Yunnan could take a stand against Japan unscathed.

Long Yun, the long-standing King of Yunnan, was no fool; he knew better than to force the people of Yunnan to die in a meaningless battle. The Imperial Japanese Army on the other hand, plagued by terrain, supply issues, and years of accumulated fatigue, were at their limit; thus both sides came to terms in order to avoid pointless bloodshed.
strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2:
But there was one variable that had yet to be resolved, that of Long Yun's Status. Entrenched influence in Yunnan after years of his reign, complicated by mutual distrust with Wang Jingwei and his Japanese masters after Long Yun followed Chiang's call to comdemn Wang's betrayal, Long Yun knew his rule would be untenable.

Therefore, he passed the position of governor to his cousin Lu Han, who was optimal for both sides of the conference table. Being less powerful and influential made him acceptable to Japan; to Long Yun, he was his cousin and longtime comrade-in-arms whom he could trust fully in all Yunnan matters. As a compromise, Long Yun would remain in the cabinet as ceremonial head of government, his cousin's second-in-command, while Lu Han officially signed a ceasefire and surrendered to the 'National Government of China'.
strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3:
Lu Han himself, once violently opposed to any concept of peace with Japanese imperialists, was more willing to compromise after being shaken by the IJA's atrocities during the War.

But Lu Han's ascension did not solve everything. After all, Long Yun was too connected to Yunnan's administration and his removal would cause massive unrest among citizens, tribes and the remnants of the military. Therefore, a compromise was reached: Long Yun would remain in the cabinet as ceremonial head of government, his cousin's second-in-command. As the new head of state, Lu Han officially signed a ceasefire and surrendered to the 'National Government of China' instead of Japan itself; this made sense given that with Chiang's death the Nanjing puppet-government was the only Chinese government that remained.
strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.4:
In 1962, Lu Han remains in power, his hold apparently secure; in fact, however, he is increasingly bedevilled by dissent and insurgencies, and the people are nowhere near as satisfied as they could be.

Several reasons exist: first, some say that the peace has corroded Lu Han's formerly strongly nationalist spirit: so long as Nanjing keeps to its promises of autonomy for him, he has no problem with continued collaboration. Second, close relationships and gifts from the local landlords - at worst flat-out bribery - make him less and less concerned about the welfare of the average people - of Yunnan. Seemingly trapped in a cycle between insurgent harassment and concessions to his Nanjing overlords for the sake of stability, some say Lu Han has drained himself of any sympathy he might've earned.
strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.5:
Lu Han, however, knew better. The IJA's atrocities during the War had shaken him to the core; since then, the fear has driven him on the search for an alternative way to unshackle China with none of the outright bloodshed. And President Gao Zongwu's Five Modernizations program, now in full swing, provides just that. A covert way to keep the Japanese at bay, and a golden opportunity to prove his loyalty - the solution that's the best of both worlds. So he exploits the Yunnan people, in the name of the welfare of China.

Deep down Lu does realize that all his harsh methods are to help China break its chains and become free at long last. But this is not obvious to most. Nor, for that matter, is it sufficient to assuage the misery of Yunnan's oppressed people.
strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.6:
No one who knows the situation as stated above is surprised when they hear that the former “King” of Yunnan, Long Yun is not happy at all. He feels that his cousin has fallen hard from grace and is no longer the honorable man he once respected.

With China's weak army and Japan's increasing collapse, Long Yun believes that a chance to pressure Nanjing to treat the southwestern peripheral areas better by force is coming ever-closer. As Long Yun's position is ceremonial, he lacks the authority to truly push the central government - not that the Japanese would allow it anyway. But that doesn't leave him powerless - not only is he still highly prestigious throughout Yunnan and beyond, but there are the insurgents... who just might be able to lend him a hand when the time comes.
strings.YUN_CountryInfo_Content_desc.7:
- Continue with Lu Han's contribution to the Modernizations.

- Read the life story of important dissenters against Lu Han's rule.

- Await the coming of a movement that might fizzle out, leave the whole nation in misery, or free China.
strings.YUN_NPA_MILITARY_COUNCIL_DESC:
Grand Marshal Long Yun has passed away, leaving China wounded but free—but the nation has now lost its hero, and the joy of victory fades and is replaced by no small amount of uncertainty.

In the aftermath of the King of Yunnan's funeral, General Song Xilian and his comrades in the National Protection Army have formed an emergency military council. They say that this will be only temporary in nature, and that Xunzheng if not Xianzheng will be brought about very quickly—but people are cynical, remembering the blunders of Chiang Kai-shek, and the fate of China has become blurry.

As Song Xilian begins the onerous task of rebuilding his country and fulfilling the legacy of his mentor the Grand Marshal, people watch with curiosity and fear—what will China become now? If Song and his closest allies have anything to say about it, however, no matter what China becomes from now on, it will at least be free. They will not let the Middle Kingdom fall to Japanese imperialism ever again.

But the doubt remains: surely there is something better than this.
strings.YUN_Long_Yun_hog_1_desc:
Head of Government
Civilian Dictatorship
--------------
The cousin of Yunnan's warlord, Long Yun settled down in the southwestern province after the fall of Chongqing made clear that further resistance to the Japanese menace would do more harm than good to China. Collaboration became a necessary evil, and Yun has since become an efficient bureaucrat and politician within the warlord state.

However, Lu Han has now taken it upon himself to exploit the Yunnanese to their limits under the guise of Pan-Asian unity, and Yunnan has found itself bleeding dry to fuel the ever demanding Reorganised Government. Something has to break soon, else Yunnan will die a death of a thousand cuts.
strings.YUN_Long_Zehui_for_desc:
Foreign Minister
Despotism
--------------
Long Zehui is no stranger to fighting the Japanese. A veteran of the Battle of Taierzhuang and the Second Sino-Japanese War, he has seen the worst the Empire has brought upon his home and lost countless friends to its roaring machine. When the peace talks were done and the war stopped, Long Zehui felt an emotion that makes him feel betrayed to the core: relief. As he shook hands and collaborated with Japan, this feeling became more and more muted, until he could easily ignore it.

Now, in Chinese Frontiers, he saw what was an easy posting, distant from the politicking of the RGOC, and most important, physically away from the Japanese officials and bureaus that strike the old fear in his heart.
Perhaps here, he can find some peace that he has been denied for two decades.
strings.YUN_Wang_Shaoyuan_eco_desc:
Economy Minister
Despotism
--------------
Yunnan is in need of help, and Wang Shaoyuan will be the one to help it. Born on January 26th in 1903, Wang grew up to be one of Yunnan's finest entrepreneurs, always willing to lend a helping hand. At the age of 17, he joined his father's company in the hopes of becoming a businessman. Seven years later, in 1927, he was appointed the Kunming Manager after a reorganization. From there, thanks to his good management, the company flourished, and grew to become the foremost international trade company in the region.

During the war against Japan, he served well supplying the National Revolutionary Army with fabric and strengthening Yunnan in the face of invasion. Now he has been called once more to provide his services for the Modernizations and against the insurgencies, and that he will. Though Yunnan is one of the weakest regions in China economically, there is potential, and it is this that Wang hopes to seize upon.
strings.YUN_Zeng_Wanzhong_sec_desc:
Security Minister
Despotism
--------------
At best, Zeng Wanzhong is an opportunist who wanted to maintain his power. At worst, a traitor to China leading an army for the sole purpose of serving another nation's interests. Born in 1894, Zeng was given proper military education and quickly rose the ranks of the National Revolutionary Army. A commander-in-chief in the Nationalists' Fifth Army, Zeng was able to see firsthand the triumph of the Japanese over China's weak and divided forces. After the Japanese victory over China seemed destined, Zeng decided to join forces with Lu Han's collaborators.

Now residing in Yunnan, Zeng has grown complacent. With the war having ended decades ago, Zeng has seen no reason to instill a sense of discipline in his troops. Lack of supervision, governance, and general structure has defined his time in post-war Yunnan. Zeng Wanzhong is old and lazy, a perfect representation of Yunnan's military.
strings.YUN_Long_Yun_hog_desc:
Head of Government
Stratocracy
--------------
Hatred is humanity's finest weapon, a lesson the Axis imposed to the world at large, and one that Long Yun has taken not only to his heart but to his gaze, posture, and words. The collaborators and the traitors stole of him everything of worth, but what he weeps most is not what he lost, but what his beloved nation lost; her pride, her people and her history have been cast into oblivion. An entire generation was raised to bow upon the Rising Sun in fear - to leech off their home's bounty and sell to foreigners their dignity for mere scraps.

With the National Protection Army under his umbrella, the lesson Japan carved in his soul will echo like a drum as the army marches on.

And upon the Begonia Leaf, Long Yun hopes to carve a second lesson to be seen by the world at large: That China will not bow to the order that Japan and their ilk imposed upon the world, that her sons and daughters will be avenged, and that, by trial, blood, tears and fury, they will be free.
strings.YUN_Song_Xilian_for_desc:
Foreign Minister
Despotism
--------------
For Song Xilian, the Second Sino-Japanese War has been raging for over two decades. Born in 1907 as a native of Hunan, he managed to get himself into the Whampoa Military Academy early on in life, becoming one of its youngest graduates. Joining the Kuomintang shortly after, Song committed his life to rising through the National Revolutionary Army's ranks. At the advent of the Second Sino-Japanese War, Song was assigned to Yunnan, fighting the war in the mountains of Western Yunnan and in the jungles of Northern Burma.

With the collapse of the central government, Song has waged a guerrilla war in Yunnan for years, although with diminishing strength and spirit. With Long Yun's rebellion in full swing, Song Xilian has found purpose once more. Joining forces with the NPA, Song now serves in face of his greatest challenge yet. China shall either be freed, or he shall die in a most heroic manner.
strings.YUN_Li_Mi_eco_desc:
Foreign Minister
Stratocracy
--------------
How does one describe Li Mi? On one side, he's been fighting for Chinese freedom for decades, and on the other, he's an opium smuggler exploiting the collapse of a nation for profit. A Yunnanese native, Li was born in 1902 and despite a rather challenging upbringing was able to obtain a modern education. Entering Whampoa Military Academy in 1924, he became fiercely loyal to both Chiang Kai-shek and the Kuomintang in general.

During the war, Li Mi fought alongside Song Xilian in Western Yunnan and after the central government's collapse, they led the remainder of their troops on a guerrilla campaign against the newly established Japanese collaborator governments. Using the complete lack of central authority and regulation, Li began smuggling opium to finance the guerrilla force, and later the NPA. Now fighting in Long Yun's National Protection Army, Li Mi is committed to seeing China united and free once more.
strings.YUN_Zhang_Chong_sec_desc:
Security Minister
Despotism
--------------
Zhang Chong: quick, agile, and bold. Those were the words that surrounded him throughout his childhood. Since his birth in 1901 in a Yunnanese village, Zhang Chong has held and kept a reputation as a quick-witted and bold man. Initially, he started out as a bandit in the chaos following Xinhai, eliminating other bandits and helping the people with more than 600 compatriots. Using this team, he also periodically raided the French-Yunnan Railway, to the anger of the French. Such actions garnered the attention of Governor Tang Jiyao, who dispatched troops to surround Zhang and, after multiple failures, eventually offered amnesty and enlistment to the man. Zhang was then recruited and was given a position in the military. As the Warlord Era raged on, Tang Jiyao was eventually overthrown in 1927, and Zhang's alliance with Long Yun against Hu Ruoyu earned him the commandership of the 5th Division at the age of 26.

During the Anti-Japanese War, the Yunnanese Army was reformed into the 60th Army and Zhang Chong served as the commander of the 184th Division. There, he fought at the famous Battle of Taierzhuang, where he made a name for himself among the National Revolutionary Army. It was from there that he was decorated for his valour, and eventually was appointed as the leader of the Third Route Army after the battle of Wuhan. As China fell around him, and as the Japanese marched in province after province, raising the flag of the Nanjing regime, Zhang Chong continued to resist; even as Yunnan surrendered and he was forced to retreat with Song Xilian's Corps, Zhang Chong continued to resist.

Now the liberation flag is raised, and the people call upon him once more. They call for him to return and fight alongside the sons of China against their oppressors. And he shall answer that call and fulfill the people's demands, or die trying.
strings.YUN_Jiang_Jingguo_hog_desc:
Head of Government
Chiang Kai-Shek Thought
--------------
For the first time since the Opium War, China has stopped bleeding. Her wounds packed with the sacrifice of millions of Chinese, the Middle Kingdom is finally free. A new dawn rises over China, and now Jiang Jingguo stands at its head.

As the son of the late Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, Jiang has returned from his long exile in the Ma Clique. When the National Protection Army swept north and the Reorganized Government collapsed, Jiang felt something stir within him. In the National Protection Army, he saw the spirit of the old United Front. Against his better judgement, Jiang threw in with the rebels in their mad crusade against Japanese Imperialism, and his gamble has paid off.

Now, the Grand Marshal is dead, and the new Chinese Republic rests in Jiang's hands. He is no fool, Jiang knows that his ascension is not due to his own merits, but due to the mystique surrounding his father. It matters not to Jiang, for the son of the Generalissimo intends to do China proud.
strings.YUN_Sun_Liren_sec_desc:
Security Minister
Military Junta
--------------
Forced out of the Chinese military following Japanese pressure as a result of his all too successful battles against the IJA during the Second Sino-Japanese War, Sun Liren settled into unquiet exile in Guangxi. Sun, however, was unable to remain still, and the ambitious officer continued to study and train in the arts of war. When the National Protection Army declared war on the Reorganized Government and added Guangxi to their list of allies, Sun saw his star blaze once again.

Serving as an officer in the NPA, Sun put his years of study and wargames to use, helping to break the Japanese stranglehold on the mainland. With the defeat of Japan on the mainland and the establishment of a free Chinese government, Zhang Xueliang recommended that Sun Liren replace the retiring Zhang Chong as security minister. Sun has taken to his new position with gusto, and dreams of building the Chinese armed forces to one day stand shoulder to shoulder with the great powers.

strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_info_tt:
Lu Han's fiefdom of landlords and lapdogs has earned itself more than its fair share of enemies over the years, and those who were brave or stupid enough to oppose us have been a considerable thorn in our side. If we hope to counter these insurgents and terrorists, we will need to root out these partisans without hesitation, and fast.

If we hope to secure Yunnan from these threats, we will need to crush them like the insects they are. There is no alternative but suppression for these insurgents via Garrisons and Police, and we will need to do whatever it takes and pay whatever misc costs the safety forces requires to secure Yunnan, lest Lu Han's regime comes to a tragic end.

However, these groups are ultimately hostile to Lu Han's collaboration instead of Xinan itself, and while Lu Han's regime seems unchallenged so far, we may find ourselves in a weaker position in case Lu Han's mandate collapses and we suppress the insurgents too harsh...
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_NRA_desc: The first group opposed to our rule are the remnants of the National Revolutionary Army along the Burma Road, which has disrupted traffic with ourselves and Burma, not to mention constantly raiding government assets and arms depots. While they are far from on track to overthrow our rule, we will need to dispose of them in due time.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_CCP_desc: The Chinese Communist Party continues to accumulate support within the rural regions, gaining popularity for their populism against our loyal landlords. While they are still largely irrelevant at present, they are still disrupting the actions of the state, and we will need to keep an eye on them, lest they grow beyond recognition.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_Bandit_desc: The bandits of the southwestern mountains have caused incredible pain for our landlords, as they have robbed our businessmen of their rightful profits. These thieves have only caused problems for the state, and they are not liable to stop until we put a stop to these activities.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_NPA_desc: The greatest threat to Lu Han's government at this point in time is not a foe from without, but an opponent from within. The NPA movement within the military and the upper administration has grown beyond belief, and continues to attempt to return China to an age of nationalism and revanchist ideals. To secure our state, we will need to put an end to this outdated belief, one way or another.

strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_NRA_tt: This will weaken NRA power but strengthen other movements. It will take 30 days before we can shift our focus.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_improve_training_desc: We have ignored our army's status for so long that they're now struggling with the NRA remnants hiding inside the mountains around our borders. Thankfully, we have plenty of officers trained under the prestiged Yunnan Military Academy and with some extra payments and promises, they will be more than willing to return and bring our forces out from such miserable status.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_improve_training_1_tt: Strengthen Garrison's effectiveness against the NRA.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_CCP_desc: We will focus on dealing with the Chinese Communist Party at the cost of ignoring the other groups temporaily.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_CCP_tt: This will weaken CPC power but strengthen other movements. It will take 30 days before we can shift our focus.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_improve_admin: Improve Our Administration in Rural Areas
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_improve_admin_desc: The CPC remnants are a formidable force to deal with becuase of their extensive connections in the rural areas: our administrative inefficiency has restricted our power projection and we fail to gather enough intel about the red menace. As such, we have to start expanding our administration in those villages we have neglected for so long. While the cities will remain our major source of wealth and resources, the majority of our population are settled in the rural areas and we can't risk to have them fall into the hands of the partisans.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_improve_admin_1_tt: Strengthen Garrison's effectiveness against the CCP.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_bandit_desc: We will focus on dealing with the bandits at the cost of ignoring the other groups temporaily.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_bandit_tt: This will weaken bandit power but strengthen other movements. It will take 30 days before we can shift our focus.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_carrot_and_stick_desc: We can't back down to the bandits in order to keep our important ties with the landlords and benefactors. However, we can perhaps provide some token promises to the poor people with minimal effects on the elites. For example - thanks to the efforts of those NSAU intellectuals, we can afford to expand our education further which will help the poor gather better skills for better treatment. Meanwhile, we should tighten up the penal system to punish those who have commit crimes harsher, as a warning to their accomplice. Together, hopefully the crime rate will start falling.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_carrot_and_stick_1_tt: Strengthen Police's effectiveness against the Bandits.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_NPA_desc: We will focus on dealing with the National Protection Army Movement at the cost of ignoring the other groups temporaily.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_focus_on_NPA_tt: This will weaken NPA power but strengthen other movements. It will take 30 days before we can shift our focus.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_enforce_police_desc: The so-called NPA, perhaps the biggest threat to Yunnan's stability, endlessly advocates standing against Nanjing and Tokyo without realizing how their reckless call for retribution will only ruin our homeland and our people. While Chairman Lu Han does feel sympathy for their anti-Japan cries, stability is above all else. In order to stop people from sympathizing and joining the NPA, our police must be enforced to shut down the dissents, and our army must be supervised more thoroughly to prevent any risk of mutiny. The less the NPA can speak, the fewer people will join their movement.
strings.YUN_insurgency_GUI_enforce_police_1_tt: Strengthen Police effectiveness against the NPA

strings.YUN_xinan_insurgency_dynamic_modifier_de: NRA, CCP, NPA, and the bandits. These insurgent groups, internally or externally, attempt to undermine Yunnan's rightful regime. Ignoring these growing rebellions is not an option: not only they are threatening our economy, but they also pose a serious threat to Lu Han's reign if we allow them to continue such treacherous behaviours...
strings.YUN_xinan_insurgency_desc:
Soon before Guizhou will finally entered a true state of union with Yunnan, a wide variety of resistance movements and partisans have come with it. From the National Revolutionary Army making pushes for the long-dead republicanism of Sun Yat-sen and Chiang Kai-shek, the masses of bandits robbing government assets, the remnants of the Chinese Communist Party along the Vietnamese border, and the NPA fighting under the banner of nationalism, Lu Han has his work cut out for him.

Assuming we have enough resources and enough time, we will find no trouble in eliminating these insurgents. Even still, we have no reason not to make a heavy push against these resistance movements, and to ensure that all of Xinan is integrated into Yunnan as soon as possible.
strings.YUN_xinan_insurgency_tt: New decision will be unlocked to tackle the resistance groups.
strings.YUN_ghost_of_the_past_desc:
Across Yunnan, covert NRA operations have been in full swing since the crushing of Chongqing and the establishment of Lu Han's rule over Yunnan. These operations were initially believed to be low-level crime and robbery, though it is now clear as to just how extensive these insurgents are within Yunnan. After some preliminary reports against the organization, it is clear as to just how powerful the NRA has become, and how much of a threat it stands to become against Lu Han's government.

Thanks to their connections within Burma and low-level government officials, not to mention currying the favor of countless landlords, the NRA partisans, perhaps the biggest external threat to the regime, have become the most influential leaders of the black market, and stand to become strong enough to rise up and cause serious trouble for Lu Han. If we strike now, however, we will be strangling this insurgency in the crib, and we will certainly manage to survive this horrible ordeal.
strings.YUN_burma_road_in_danger_desc:
A constant threat to the Burma Road has always been - and continues to be - the NRA. Like an insufferable cancer that knows no bounds, the NRA has been feeding off of the Burma Road to sell their own goods and profit off of whatever they can steal. Not a month ago, the NRA had blown up a convoy making its way from the Azad Hind government. This is far from the beginning and is far from the end. Even still, it can mark the beginning of the end.

We will redouble our efforts to secure the Burma Road. Between providing additional garrisons and cracking down on known cells, this will do nothing short of obliterate the regional NRA. That is the hope, and should our troops do their job, we only have reason to believe these operations will succeed.
strings.YUN_send_soldiers_to_border_desc:
It seems as though with every strike made against the NRA insurgents, with every revealed outpost and exhausted patrol, the republicans come back with redoubled resources and redoubled spirits. As of our most recent reports, the NRA seem to be concentrating much of their renewed manpower on the Burma Road, most likely in an effort to recommence their countless black market operations to regain their lost power. If we act fast, however, we may have no reason to fear these developments.

By increasing our presence along the border with Burma - as well as our total present troops within the Burma Road itself - we will not only counteract the growing NRA presence but also manage to turn the tide against this disruptive republicanism. With a bit of luck and skill, of course.
strings.YUN_contact_burma_for_coop_desc:
We cannot strike the NRA alone, certainly not with the limited power within our jurisdiction. As a result, our wisest leader, Lu Han, has made an effort to reach out to the Burmese government, coordinate a properly coordinated force against the NRA, and secure the Burma Road. Should all go to plan, we will be able to use the combined powers of the Yunnan and Burmese armies.

It is imperative that this meeting goes to plan. Should we fail to coordinate a sizable force capable of crushing the NRA, then we are liable to lose out on money not only being taken out of our pockets, but the NRA will also gain a considerable foothold in the region. While far from a death blow, we will certainly be set back on our efforts, which is something we cannot afford.
strings.YUN_the_red_menace_desc:
There are few enemies to Lu Han who are as popular among the rural populace as the remnants of the Chinese Communist Party. Even as the movement has been crushed twice before, it seems as though it is high time that the CPC is crushed a third time by the hand of Lu Han, if that is what it takes. While the CPC has proven to be among the trickiest resistance groups of China, their methods of opposing the government have grown predictable. Exploiting these patterns will prove essential to securing Yunnan.

As the CPC has proven itself competent at bringing rural regions to its side, it is high time that extra garrisons are posted to the region. Cracking down on these operations from the CPC will only strengthen Lu Han's position within Yunnan, and Yunnan will only become stronger as a result. If all goes to plan, there won't be any need to worry over these communists, and the vast, sprawling lands of Yunnan and Xinan will only be mended closer together.
strings.YUN_the_horror_of_partisans_desc:
The Chinese Communist Party has always provided our troops with a near-impossible challenge with every engagement they begin, which is exactly what causes our brave soldiers so much trouble - they're never the first to start a fight. The CPC forces have always been the first to strike, and it has only caused tragedy for our troops on the ground. Ambush after ambush, and all our soldiers can do is fight back with useless volleys of inadequate gunfire. What can we do, then?

If our methods are useless or inadequate, it is high time we do what we can to change them. Unfortunately, we may not be able to. If we found a way to counter these partisan tactics, we would need to rewrite the combat doctrine for anti-partisan soldiers. If we had a doctrine to redistribute, we would need to retrain our troops in a project of unparalleled scale. As a result, there is little which can be done against these insurgents, not to say we won't try.
strings.YUN_establish_rural_area_network_desc:
If we ever hope to put a firm stop to the Chinese Communist Party's activities, we must do whatever we can to halt their growth. While our efforts to combat these threats have been increasingly effective, it is nowhere near fast enough to properly combat the unrestrained growth of the CCP's forces. While we may not be able to halt the growth of resistance by actively combating it, we may still be able to cut off this snake at its head.

Through establishing connections within the rural communities in which the CPC flourishes in, we will be able to infiltrate these insurgents and cause chaos within their ranks. While far from a permanent solution, it will allow us to also identify future attacks against government assets. It will take time, but we are certainly cutting down these communists. It is far from the end, but we are beginning to see the light at the end of the tunnel.
strings.YUN_contact_vietnam_desc:
A nation in a situation considerably similar to our own, Vietnam, has been entrenched in a partisan war notably similar to our own. Both of our nations have been caught grinding down on these communist partisans, and it is believed that many of our shared problems may be sharing leaders, as well. While Bao Dai has been caught in this war just as we have, and seems to be working with similar proficiency, we would be wasting an opportunity to share information and fighting tactics.

In this war against the Chinese Communist Party, we will need as much help as we can get. It goes without saying that this insurgency is weakening our government's hold over rural regions, and we may soon have no choice but to end this war and fast.
strings.YUN_contact_vietnam_tt: As useless as Bao Dai is, at least he can take some nominal actions against the Viet Cong that can slightly improve the effectiveness of our countermeasures against the CCP...
strings.YUN_bandits_of_the_southwest_desc:
Throughout the mountains of southwestern Yunnan, there lays a despicable disease to Yunnan, which has only grown in size since it was first identified nearly twenty years ago, as an order within Yunnan first faded, and gave way to widespread banditry in the uncrossable lands of the mountains and rivers of the Southwest. These blights on both humanity and Yunnan have done nothing but disrupt our economy, and threaten the lives of our landlords. This ends now.

It will be a long, hard campaign, but it must be done if we hope for our most loyal landlords to remain safe and happy. By beginning a series of anti-terrorist operations in the Southwest, we will begin the long process of properly uprooting these bandits from Yunnan. All it will take is time.
strings.YUN_land_of_thefts_desc:
Of all the vital gears in the great machine of Lu Han's Yunnan, there are few as influential or profitable as the humble landlord. Having done more than their fair share for the economic prosperity of Yunnan, it goes without saying that those within our territories who hold the title of a landlord are more than within their rights to demand protection and security. In light of the bandit epidemic across Yunnan, it is high time that we fulfill our promises to these landlords.

Through cooperating with the afflicted landlords and further cracking down on these glorified thieves, we're liable to burn right through this little problem of banditry.
strings.YUN_one_more_bandit_hunt_desc:
Our past actions against the bandits of the Southwest have been effective. There is a marked decrease in banditry within the mountains, and our loyal landlords are reporting fewer and fewer armed robberies. Even still, it is not enough.

With every bandit arrested or shot, there seems to be another dozen that pop out of the mountains. Why this is, of course, is still up to debate, though now is not the time to debate such non-issues. What is in need of addressing is the ever-increasing banditry. As we stifle the bandits on the streets, and more come up to replace each arrested felon, it is clear that we must redouble our efforts to crush these criminals. By incentivizing the police to increase their focus on the bandits, we will surely find the bandits to die off like the fading disease that they are.
strings.YUN_show_no_mercy_desc:
Across all of Yunnan, our efforts to crush the NRA, CCP, Bandits, and NPA have all shown limited success at best. While we do seem to be wearing down the dissidents at a considerable rate, it is proving far from fast enough to keep the dissidents down. Should we really want to purge Yunnan of these insurgents, we will need to do everything in our power to rid ourselves of the terrorists. Everything. We have already reworked our tactics time and time again, we have already put our loyal troops on high alert, and we have already done everything that we can.

Our troops, then, must be the ones to do more for Yunnan.

Our current restrictions for the troops are more or less already loosely enforced, though they are far from harsh enough to deal with the countless insurgents. We are far past the time for mercy. No matter what it takes, we will secure Yunnan.
strings.YUN_show_no_mercy_tt: We will loosen the restrictions placed upon garrisons and police forces, strengthening their effectiveness against the threats.
strings.YUN_the_warmongers_desc:
An unfortunate, ever-persistent aspect of the psyche of much of the Chinese military has been the notion of nationalism and revanchism against Japan and the East Asian Co-Prosperity Sphere. This insubordination has been spreading under the organization of the NPA and shows nearly no signs of stopping. But bluntly, the belief has refused to die within our ranks. Our objective is now to kill it.

This belief has been a thorn in the side of the peace-loving Lu Han and has only served as a terrible memory of the worst that China has to offer the Co-Prosperity Sphere. With some work, bullets, and sweat, however, we will find Yunnan to be more loyal to the Co-Prosperity Sphere than ever before.
strings.YUN_revanchism_in_xinan_desc:
As thanks to our recent unification with Xinan, we have found ourselves in the company of a great many bureaucrats and generals who had not prior adhered to our strict ideological regimentation. While this is obviously quite a blow to both our efforts of integration and our efforts of appeasing Japan, we may find a middle ground that can allow for us to play the Japanese and these nationalistic elements off of each other.

Assuming we can find a way to keep the most extreme elements of these forces at bay, we can both lessen the influence of the pro-Japanese forces, as well as maintain some modicum of autonomy for Yunnan.

It is a fine line which Lu Han walks, between the nationalists and Japanophiles. Should he play his cards right, however, he may walk away without even the thought of any opposition to his rule.
strings.YUN_purge_the_military_desc:
While the revanchist and nationalistic aspects of the Yunnan army have proven a strong counterbalance to Japanese influence, the most vocal elements are proving a clear threat to Lu Han's government. With each passing day that these radical officials and generals remain in the government, more and more upstanding individuals are being tricked into the notion of opposition to the Co-Prosperity Sphere. This can obviously not stand.

If we hope to maintain the stability of Yunnan, we will need to put these officials down like the rabid dogs they are. While we cannot outright execute many of these individuals, as they are far too popular and influential even behind bars, they can be taken out of the picture for the foreseeable future. Should this effort succeed, the NPA movement will be crippled, and Yunnan's military will be put back on the right path.
strings.YUN_end_reactionary_thoughts_desc:
The only way we can put a proper and complete end to the NPA movement is if it is stopped in its tracks. Of everything which we will need to do to ensure the security of the Yunnan army, maintaining control over those within our ranks will be the absolute priority. Through bugging the offices of our high command, hiring tails for those who we remain suspicious of, and encouraging new recruits to report suspicious behaviour of senior members, Yunnan will be made infinitely safer than when crawling with traitors.

These actions will only strengthen Yunnan as a whole, no matter the measures which we are forced to implement. Even if those within the army grow angry, they will be reassured by the fact that this is all in the name of Yunnan's national security.
strings.YUN_end_reactionary_thoughts_tt: We will grant the police force more freedom to crush the movement, strengthening their effectiveness against the NPA.
strings.YUN_peace_in_our_time_desc:
Within the government of Yunnan, there is a growing sense of relief and desperation. Everything which has been done to put an end to the insurgencies across Yunnan is coming to a head. They need to, after all, as we are running out of alternatives. It seems as though the last tricks up our sleeve have been exhausted, the knives we have used against the terrorists dulled, and the reserves of the police and anti-terrorist forces finally becoming depleted. At this point, we have no alternative but to have put an end to the majority of the insurgencies, otherwise, we are in serious trouble.

All we can do now is close our eyes and hope. Hope that enough has been done, hope that the armies have done enough, hope that Yunnan will survive. As much we can hope for. It will become clear with time. All we know is that we have done our best, whether or not it was enough.
strings.YUN_Long_Yun_Coup_tt: The King of Yunnan has returned since his exile from his rightful throne. Today, history will be reshaped and China will never be the same again.
strings.YUN_ROC_reborn_tt: With one heart and one virtue, may we carry through the principles until the very end.
strings.YUN_bandit_holdouts_desc: Despite our best efforts to purge the villainous scum from our fair land, they still persist. Hidden in the caverns of mountains, nestled into the bushes, and in every alleyway, bandits and thieves scope out their next target.
strings.YUN_hidden_potential_0_desc: The Chinese Southwest is a region rich in various mineral resource deposits - deposits that lie unused. If we were to find a way to make use of our mineral wealth, Yunnan could become a prosperous little statelet within the Co-Prosperity Sphere...
strings.YUN_hidden_potential_1_desc: Our initial report was far from accurate. There are more resources hidden under our feet than once thought. We are already in the process of offering contracts to companies to begin the excavation.
strings.YUN_hidden_potential_2_desc: The profits have begun to trickle in, providing us with the means to further expand our operations! Money is not everything however, the resources found under our soil are critical for the construction of the common goods of the modern world!
strings.YUN_hidden_potential_3_desc: The mountains and caverns never cease to surprise us, once it seems that we have plundered one region for all of its worth, a mine with ten times the production springs up. Yunnan offers us much for our fair treatment of the land.
strings.YUN_hidden_potential_4_desc: Since the birth of civilization, people have inhabited the region of modern day Yunnan. Cultivating crops, founding families, solidifying society, all advances made from the land of Yunnan. Our next advancement has arrived, Yunnan ushers us once more into the future. With our profits, we are rapidly becoming the envy of the Sphere.
strings.YUN_hidden_potential_5_desc: Riches abound! Yunnan ranks first in the Sphere in deposits of zinc, lead, tin and we can hardly rip it from the ground fast enough to please our buyers!
strings.YUN_army_of_the_southwest_desc: While Yunnan and Guizhou are nominally two separate states, this does not apply to their militaries. As He Yingqin manages the civilian affairs of Guizhou separately, Lu Han's Army of the Southwest provides the province's military protection. As such, it is not surprising to see Lu Han tighten his grip over Guizhou ever more...
strings.YUN_army_of_the_southwest_two_brothers_d: The Two Brothers of the Southwest are united at last, and the military is no exception to the benefits of regional unity.
strings.YUN_GUI_army_of_the_southwest_centralise: Xinan possesses a centralized military structure, with no division between Yunnan and Guizhou. This strong organization places power directly in the hands of Lu Han.
strings.YUN_GUI_army_of_the_southwest_decentrali: Xinan possesses a decentralized military structure, with numerous division between Yunnan and Guizhou. This weak organization takes power away from Lu Han, but ensures that the military can adapt to the unique realities of each region..
strings.YUN_Slave_revolt_0_desc: Disdain for our government is at an all time high, our policies have alienated a significant portion of the population who have taken up arms against our government. Luckily, this group is mostly splinted and unorganized.
strings.YUN_Slave_revolt_1_desc: As more are liberated by rioting slaves, their ranks grow larger and more organized. Something must be done of the situation before our nation is ripped into between the slaves and their former masters!
strings.YUN_Slave_revolt_2_desc: The population is in open revolt. Government buildings have been contorted into makeshift fortresses, preparing for the siege from the slaves. We are running out of time before we are forced to accept that our dominance was but a facade.
strings.YUN_Slave_patrols_desc: Yunnan is not a nation of dense infrastructure, of bustling cities and highways from one end to the other. It is a mountainous and spread out group of communities. To keep this vast land under our control and out of the hands of escaped slaves, government sponsored search parties roam the countryside, seeking those seeking freedom.
strings.YUN_a_government_of_friends_0_desc:
The formation of this new Congress to represent the concerns of our deeply valued and esteemed landlord class has had one major beneficial impact: a further strengthening of our bond with the élite of Yunnan. Landlords help advise our decision-making, and we receive richly-deserved funds and favours in return - what a fruitful cooperation this is!

More and more of our ministers and civil servants are retiring to join the landlord class, while landlords are increasingly our first choice in recruitment. We are creating a government of friends who can all be trusted to represent the interests of our people. Through this Yunnan will become wealthier and stronger.
strings.YUN_exploit_mines_0_desc: Our exploitation of the mineral wealth in Yunnan is still in the early stages. While there are plans to open new mines and expand existing ones, we are already seeing decent returns on our current mining development. We must be careful not to let greed blind us to the consequences of our actions.
strings.YUN_exploit_mines_1_desc: Our exploitation of the mineral wealth in Yunnan is getting out of hand. While we are getting increased returns from our expanded mining operations, there's the growing concern that we are getting too dependent on it. We need to strike a balance between our mining operations and the needs of our local industrial manufacturing sector.
strings.YUN_exploit_mines_2_desc: Our exploitation of the mineral wealth in Yunnan has gotten out of control. Open air mines dot the landscape of Yunnan, and the local industry is suffering as a result. We are getting increased returns from our expanded mining operations, but the cost is a marked decrease of our industrial productivity.
strings.YUN_investment_boom_desc:
As a result of the success of our advertisement campaign throughout the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, our state is now undergoing a fortuitous investment boon. More and more financial resources are being poured into the treasured ore and mineral resources of the Great Southwest.

And it makes very good sense - in fact, some investors tell us, the choice is really a no-brainer. How could any East Asian investor with a functioning brain ignore the treasures in our mountains? What financially literate person would let a stable opportunity like this go to waste?

Then let more money come, and let Yunnan profit from it.
strings.YUN_econ_links_CHI_desc:
Diplomacy is a terribly, terribly costly business, and some of our bureaucrats are maybe a bit too preoccupied with that fact. They've been griping to us about how the Governor is apparently “wasting money” on talks, parties, and suitable dress for negotiations with our overlord in Nanjing.

What abject nonsense! These fools don't realize how profitable our economic cooperation with Nanjing is. With the new deal being signed, we'll finally get a return on our blood, sweat, and tears: Nanjing will get the resources they need to modernize China, and we in turn get enough capital to develop Xinan and develop it well. This is a mutually profitable agreement, and one that no one with any sense will refuse—and thanks to it, Xinan is one step closer to prosperity.
strings.YUN_mild_corruption_desc:
We've decided to hand more political power and privilege to our esteemed friends, the landlords. As they have helped us govern and profit off of the province of Yunnan this entire time, as well as preserve its stability against the communist and ultranationalist rebels in the countryside, they are the natural choice to advise us in important matters.

Our cooperation will bring Yunnan to a new age of prosperity.
strings.YUN_the_mad_king: Legacy of the National Protection War
strings.YUN_the_mad_king_tenacity: Legacy of the National Protection War
strings.YUN_the_mad_king_desc:
Five decades ago, Yunnan was a mere insignificant rural backwater known only for a specific kind of tea that a narrow group of people inhaled like air. Yet despite that it was from here that Marshal Cai E, guardian of the Republic, revolted against the “Chinese Empire” and summoned people from Qinghai to Quanzhou to defeat Yuan Shikai's daydream of occupying the throne of the Qing.

Today, the legacy will be reborn. As Cai E defeated Yuan Shikai, so Grand Marshal Long Yun will lead the Chinese people in crushing the Setting Sun's fantasies of European-style colonialism and Nanjing's delusional collaborationism. Under Long Yun's leadership the Second National Protection War will bring freedom and liberation to China, and Yunnan shall be marked in history as the guardian of the Republic once more.
strings.YUN_the_mad_king_tenacity_desc:
Five decades ago, Yunnan was a mere insignificant rural backwater known only for a specific kind of tea that a narrow group of people inhaled like air. Yet despite that it was from here that Marshal Cai E, guardian of the Republic, revolted against the “Chinese Empire” and summoned people from Qinghai to Quanzhou to defeat Yuan Shikai's daydream of occupying the throne of the Qing.

Today, the legacy will be reborn. As Cai E defeated Yuan Shikai, so Grand Marshal Long Yun will lead the Chinese people in crushing the Setting Sun's fantasies of European-style colonialism and Nanjing's delusional collaborationism. Under Long Yun's leadership the Second National Protection War will bring freedom and liberation to China, and Yunnan shall be marked in history as the guardian of the Republic once more.
strings.YUN_production_frenzy_desc:
During the misrule of Lu Han, the factories were run by and for greedy colonists who exploited Xinan's wealth to no end. Resources flowed out of our homeland to the Three Pearls, to Tokyo, to Nanjing—and in the meantime, the hundred surnames kept slaving away, merely producing goods for those who regarded their interests as beneath them.

This must never happen again! With the return of the King of Yunnan, the workers in the lands of the National Protection Army will work first and foremost for the survival of the people and the liberation of China. Every factory without exception must be repurposed for weapons production; we might not match the quality of Nanjing and Japan, but we are more than capable of compensating for that through quantity.
strings.YUN_NBIS_desc:
Lu Han and his assorted sycophants and collaborators have made clear to us that the times are dark, and the minds of people have darkened to match them. The way in which we had to deal with his assorted accessories gives us pause: how many more Nanjing loyalists or potential defectors are burrowed away within our government? Something must be done.

Chiang Kai-shek was a terrible ruler and a tyrant, and Dai Li a monstrous, shameless subhuman, but between the two of them clearly knew at least some things about stabilizing their rule. The NBIS must be brought back into service—yes, we realize Chunfeng's methods are dishonorable and must be thrown out the moment Liberation is attained. But they are exactly what we need to cleanse our government of Hanjian and Japanophiles.
strings.YUN_NBIS_upgrade_desc:
Lu Han and his assorted sycophants and collaborators have made clear to us that the times are dark, and the minds of people have darkened to match them. The way in which we had to deal with his assorted accessories gives us pause: how many more Nanjing loyalists or potential defectors are burrowed away within our government? Something must be done.

Chiang Kai-shek was a terrible ruler and a tyrant, and Dai Li a monstrous, shameless subhuman, but between the two of them clearly knew at least some things about stabilizing their rule. The NBIS must be upgraded—though it disgusts us, its methods are exactly what we need to cleanse our government of Hanjian and Japanophiles.
strings.YUN_down_with_the_traitors_idea_desc:
Lu Han and his assorted sycophants and collaborators have made clear to us that the times are dark, and the minds of people have darkened to match them. The way in which we had to deal with his assorted accessories gives us pause: how many more Nanjing loyalists or potential defectors are burrowed away within our government? Something must be done.

Chiang Kai-shek was a terrible ruler and a tyrant, and Dai Li a monstrous, shameless subhuman, but between the two of them clearly knew at least some things about stabilizing their rule. The NBIS must be brought back into service—yes, we realize Chunfeng's methods are dishonorable and must be thrown out the moment Liberation is attained. But they are exactly what we need to cleanse our government of Hanjian and Japanophiles.
strings.YUN_fortification_frenzy_desc:
War is coming, as we well know. But Sunzi spoke wisely when he said that only a fool would attack without first fortifying his own position. Xinan must protect itself from the assorted Tokyo-aligned traitors in Nanjing and elsewhere. Instead of mining to support imperialists, colonists, and mentally deficient collaborators, our skillful workers should be sent to build fortifications on the borders.

Bunkers, trenches, underground networks—everything that works and can be held up by the materials we have available must be built; any cost is worth paying, any labor worth doing, if it turns Yunnan into an iron land impenetrable by any force of “Co-Prosperity” arms. In the past we dug for profit; now, let us dig for our survival!
strings.YUN_mountain_people_idea_desc:
Our people, having dealt with more than their fair share of the cruelty of humanity and nature alike, are acclimatized to difficult conditions and hard fights. Tough, cunning, and determined, our recruits have superior training and better mettle than the alleged “veterans” in Nanjing.

Even before the formations of Xinan became the nucleus of the National Protection Army, they were as strong as the Himalayas and as forceful as the avalanches that torment the hundred surnames of Xinan too often for our liking. Our army is an immovable object in defense, an unstoppable force in attack; our feeble enemies will understand this at the cost of their treasonous lives.
strings.YUN_hit_and_run_idea_desc:
Yes, it is true that bandits are those that, as Xunzi has said, succumbed to the evil inherent in their human natures and exploited other people for profit. But even such people have their uses. If there is one thing that bandits can teach our soldiers in matters of battle, it is the surpassing importance of agility and mobility—of striking the enemy's weaknesses from unknown directions, then escaping to places unseen with a backup plan in place in case of failure.

Our honorable soldiers have been fighting against these bandits for years, and they have every right to hold them in distaste. But desperate times require desperate measures. We should invite some of the more palatable bandits to teach our soldiers to fight more flexibly and therefore to avoid unnecessary sacrifices.
strings.YUN_anti_japanese_zeal_desc:
Accursed be the rotten Sun of Japan, the prime culprit of every tragedy in this land of China for the last sixty years! Accursed especially be the disgusting, shameless Emperor, who like all his bloated, incestuous ancestors falsely promotes himself as the son of the nonexistent Solar Goddess! Death and damnation to the followers of the false god in Tokyo, idiots, barbarians, and subhuman brutes all, who bring pain and misery to every land under the evil Rising Sun flag!

There can be only one simple directive for the National Protection Army: destroy every sign of this filthy symbol. Flags, portraits, and all those maniacs who, refusing to throw down their arms, continually fight under this “Hinomaru” crapshit. Only when the Army of Xinan can wipe out every Hinomaru it sees on the mainland and in Taiwan will China have a chance to be free.
strings.YUN_unrestrained_warfare_desc:
Despite our best efforts, the new recruits of the National Protection Army are still reluctant to certain aspects of our great struggle and hesitant to execute certain orders. While they hate the Japanese and the Hanjian, they are still not quite ready to embrace the idea of total war.

If we promise them the wealth of Japan in their pockets and the blood of the Japanese on their hands, they may be keener to see battle undertaken. Long Yun does not need to know this, let him think his speeches are all his men need, but we know that man cannot live on ideology alone.
strings.YUN_repair_focus_desc:
Our enemies, in their laughable, pitiful rout, have left us tremendous resources that, they were convinced, were nothing more than useless scraps. What fools! Clearly, they did not understand that the people directed by Grand Marshal Long are too resourceful to waste these treasures.

Weapons, factories, railways—so what if they have been scrapped or sabotaged? Let our army, backed as always by the people, repair them. They do not need to be perfect, just good enough to serve during the war and help us drive the Japanese imperialist bastards out of China.
strings.YUN_new_lands_desc:
The people of Yunnan are not the only ones who have suffered under the yoke of the Japanese. As we march to liberate China from the occupiers and the Hanjian, we're starting to see the brutality of the Japanese occupation in other provinces. The people of Guangxi, Guizhou, and Sichuan are all suffering under the yoke of the Japanese, and they are starting to see us as their liberators.

We must not let this opportunity go to waste. We must make sure that we are seen as liberators, not conquerors. We must make sure that we are seen as the ones who will bring prosperity and freedom from the Japan to the people of China. Only then will the once apathetic people of China rise up and join us in our struggle.
strings.YUN_unite_southwest_diplo_dynamic_modifi: With the Southwest reunified under one government, order has been restored to the region. No more will Xinan be divided between different governments, only one authority will rule the land. Yunnan and Guizhou are both a single state, with one government, one army, and one leader, and no one shall separate this union.
strings.YUN_xinan_development_dynamic_modifier_d: Ever since its conquest under the Ming dinasty, the Southwest was always neglected and central authority always struggled to keep order in the region. A land of conquest and exploitation, Xinan must catch up economically with the rest of China if we want to prove it is not an impoverished backwater, and gain the people's trust in our government.
strings.YUN_burma_road_construction_dynamic_modi: The Burma Road is a roadway connecting Myanmar with southwestern China. It was built by the British to convey supplies to China during the war in Asia, and as such it was destroyed by Japanese bombings. Today the road is still in disrepair and became the hideout of smugglers, terrorists, and NRA remnants. If we manage to rebuild the road, not only will we bring order to the region, we will also reconnect China to southeast Asia and reap the trade profits.
strings.YUN_burma_road_reward_dynamic_modifier_d: After long, hard months of labor, the Burma Road has finally been restored to its former glory. Hundreds of miles of paved roads and robust bridges are making the lives of people living in Yunnan and Myanmar easier than ever, from the growth of trade in southeast Asia to the increase in movement of people across borders. This shining example of Pan-Asian unity will stand for centuries to come.
strings.YUN_NPA_legitimacy_dynamic_modifier_desc: Just as the ancient Mandate of Heaven, legitimacy is crucial to gather the support of our people and it is important to solidify our legitimacy in people's eyes. Our regime will be more legal if we can win over the de facto independent warlords to our side, retake the rightful Chinese states and implement less militarized policies to our people.
strings.YUN_NPA_war_buff_dynamic_modifier_desc: As we achieve more and more victories as well as completing the wargoals, the NPA will be more invigorated by the victories against the weak Setting Sun and its pitful puppets. Moreover, our soldiers will be more prepared for war if we can establish a highly militarized reign in our states.
strings.YUN_in_the_west_desc: Without the aid of the capital and below the notice of the Japanese, the people of the Southwest must fend for themselves. In the mountains and fields we have only ourselves to turn to for justice, order and progress, and it is Lu Han to whom we turn.
strings.YUN_everything_for_my_friends_desc: It is only natural that those who would play such a prominent role in both the stability and advancement of Yunnan would be rewarded in turn. Lu Han would not even think of his good friends and allies having anything less than the first pick of the province. After all, they earned it.
strings.YUN_the_law_for_my_enemies_desc: Slander and lies have no place in Yunnan, at least not when they are in opposition to the government. The law is quite clear about what happens to those found guilty of... whatever the courts find them guilty of. And the courts know their duty well.
strings.YUN_minerals_for_those_who_can_pay: Minerals For Those Who Can Pay
strings.YUN_minerals_for_those_who_can_pay_desc: Yunnan has been blessed with an abundance of resources lying within the ground, and cursed with a drought of cash with which to access it. A newly discovered deposit may send investors scurrying to Lu Han to gain his favor and slander their opponents, but in the end Lu Han must accept payment from where the capital flows, so long as it does flow.
strings.YUN_crush_the_rats_desc: With this victory the last challenge to Lu's authority will be crushed. With this victory the army will be truly united. With this victory the Southwest, long divided, may finally come together in unity. Perhaps even in reality, as well as spirit. So now charge, and crush these parasites to dust!
strings.YUN_the_two_brothers_desc: Like brothers Yunnan and Guizhou have stood together against anarchy, against secession, and like brothers they have come to love each other and cooperate in everything. One army, one China, one spirit... why not one ruler as well? The unification of our two states is only natural, and as Lu Han puts his sights on this worthy goal there is no one who can stop him.
strings.YUN_evict_he_yingqin_desc: He's recent relaxation of power has proven that the old man is on his last legs, and we can no longer rely on him to ensure order and progress in the southwest. Simply removing He Yingqin from office will be fast and painless, not to mention little more than an official recognition of reality. The army and people are ours, and now the land shall be as well.
strings.YUN_setting_the_trap_desc: He Yingqin has retreated into his study for who knows what purpose, protected only by a tiny personal staff. With only one road in and out it makes for the perfect place to pin down He and ensure that the consolidation goes off without a hitch. Sending out a few scouts and obtaining the blueprints of his estate should be all that is necessary to prepare the trap.
strings.YUN_setting_the_trap_tt: We should prepare a stockpile of equipment and armaments before planning out the operation.
strings.YUN_pick_up_his_friends_desc: He is hardly the only man in Guizhou who demands our attention, indeed the few officers disloyal to Lu Han and the men of means must either be bribed or otherwise neutralized during the merger. Of course, it would not do to be disrespectful to men of such standing, we merely want them to understand that now would be an excellent time to vacation.
strings.YUN_a_mans_home: A Man's Home Is His Castle
strings.YUN_a_mans_home_desc: The trap is ready! Men wait only for our orders to advance and surround He Yingqin's estate. We can only hope that He himself will be forthcoming in bowing to the inevitable. If he does not, then we shall see how strong his walls truly are. For the southwest! For Lu Han!
strings.YUN_safe_and_sound_desc: He is too dangerous to let out of our sight, even if he is weak. Thankfully we have a prison in Heqing just for people like him. Alongside the likes of Long Yun and Xue Yue He Yingqin will be kept perfectly impotent for the rest of his days, as China moves on without him.
strings.YUN_out_of_sight_out_of_mind: Out of Sight, Out of Mind
strings.YUN_out_of_sight_out_of_mind_desc: He is too dangerous to keep within our lands, even if he is a fool. We should acquire a comfortable and secure method of removing He from his old powerbase and into the new world of obscurity. A few conversations with the RGOC officials should be more than enough to make the trip quick and easy.
strings.YUN_a_formal_announcement_desc: With He Yingqin removed and the two provinces of Yunnan and Guizhou firmly under Lu Han's control all that remains is for the formal announcement of the creation of Asia's newest state: Xinan. At the head of his closest officers Lu Han made his speech, and soon correspondence with the rest of the sphere shall notify all.
strings.YUN_one_and_indivisible_desc: On this day, in this place, the lands once known as Yunnan and Guizhou were finally united under the benevolent guidance of Lu Han and took for themselves a new name: Xinan. Long may she live and may her people know prosperity and peace for all of their days. And what has been brought together let no man part.
strings.YUN_we_are_not_enemies_desc: While the unification of our two states is inevitable, the process must not be marred with violence, which would betray the friendship between our two states. Instead we shall look into more peaceful and civilized ways to bring our few opponents to our point of view and work with He rather than against him.
strings.YUN_arranging_a_conference_desc: Talking may be a boring and lengthy process, but no one can doubt that it is at least cheaper than war. Arranging a date and location for the “Discussion of the Future of the Southwest Provinces” is of course only the first step, but no doubt it will take time to arrange a venue deserving of this momentous occasion.
strings.YUN_winning_friends_desc: Lu Han has many friends, and he knows just how to keep them: money. It seems that in his recent relaxation He Yingqin has been forgetful of his old friends, a mistake that Lu promises will not be repeated under his supervision. Meeting with industrialists, politicians, landlords, and even an artist has consumed Lu Han's time; it would not do to be impersonal at this time.
strings.YUN_opening_the_debate_desc: A city has been chosen, and invitations sent out. Delegates carefully chosen for their enthusiasm for unification shall of course form the body, and despite He's lone resistance the debate shall soon be started with or without him and the few friends he has left. It has been made clear that it would be better to have his voice be present at negotiations, rather than not be present at all.
strings.YUN_two_hands_of_one_body_desc: While Yunnan and Guizhou may be brothers in all but name, their economies have developed in different directions by necessity, with different companies taking different approaches to the exploitation of China's resources. While the idea of economic uniformity may be romantic, for the sake of common prosperity we should make the merger be one of politics only, and let the market continue its own course.
strings.YUN_closed_to_yi_exploitation_desc: The people of Guizhou are sadly less enthusiastic about the incoming unification than we are, with rumours abounding about plans to enslave and exploit the people, and bloody crackdowns on disent. Simply promising not to alter the laws of the land would go a long way toward calming the people and ensuring the merger is as successful as possible.
strings.YUN_a_place_for_he_desc: He was and is a great general, a competent administrator, and he knows the province of Guizhou better than any other man in China. While he agrees to step down as a provincial governor, installing He Yingqin as governor or regional advisor would guarantee a swift and seemly transition of power as well as pay respect to He's service to the country and her people.
strings.YUN_united_economy_desc: No split may divide the Southwest, no artificial barriers may stop unification. While keeping the economies unintegrated may let a few fat cats keep their riches it will also permanently divide the new province. What is the point of going to all this trouble if nothing of substance changes? Not to mention, the unification has gotten up the hopes of many of our own Yi entrepreneurs who would be very disappointed should the unification be only in name.
strings.YUN_uniform_legal_code_desc: Break one law? Just hope over the border and you are scot free! Chaos in trade, in the media, in everyday life is the only reward for being so lazy as to unify without actually unifying! The laws of Yunnan were approved by Lu Han himself, and were virtually identical to Guizhou's until recent years. We would be doing a disservice by accepting anything less than total uniformity.
strings.YUN_he_must_retire_desc: No one doubts He Yingqin's record in the past and we have much to thank him for. But in recent years he has become reserved, retreating into his palace and delegating ever more authority to those unworthy of it. Not to mention, should He remain in power all those who would resist this merging of provinces will rally to him, whether he desires it or not. An honorable retirement is in order, but He must go.
strings.YUN_a_handshake_desc: With the debate over all that is left is for the vote on integration. Most consider it to be a foregone conclusion, but before the votes are counted all eyes are on He Yingqin and Lu Han, to seal the arrangement with a handshake.
strings.YUN_a_ceremony_desc: The die is cast, and the map will be redrawn! Let all of Asia know: The provinces of Yunnan and Guizhou shall, by mutual agreement, soon be merged into the province of the southwest: Xinan. The start of this new era has been accompanied by parades, bands, grand dinners, and all the other melodrama of state. Let the people rejoice!
strings.YUN_a_promise_desc: With the announcement over and the deadline drawing near it is only expected that those patriots who bravely aided the creation of Xinan be rewarded in turn. And they all intend to ensure Lu Han is aware of that fact. Land, gold, currency, positions in the administration and protection from the free market has all been promised. And what kind of man would Lu be if he were not true to his word?
strings.YUN_united_at_last_desc: The final disruptions are over, the names have been changed and the world notified. All that is left now is for Lu Han himself to make the trip and officially declare the work of government to begin. Two brothers no more, today the name Xinan shall be spoken across all of Asia, and let no man separate what has been unified!
strings.YUN_on_solid_ground_desc: At long last our hopes have become reality. Yunnan and Guizhou are both under the rule of Lu Han, and the Yunnan clique has come to protect another province. While we faced unrest and protest from some the result was never truly in doubt: one state, one army, one leader. As the maps are redrawn and streets renamed we are finally in a position to advance with order and progress unimpeded.
strings.YUN_bring_in_the_investment_desc: Perhaps unavoidably investment both from outside individuals and our own native entrepreneurs ground to a halt in the recent instability. Now that our state is settled it is time to announce ourselves open to investment from all the Sphere. Many local monopolies and leftovers of He's rule have to be removed from the stage, and the time has never been better for the development of the land or the prosperity of all Asia!
strings.YUN_bring_in_the_talent_desc: Whether from the esteemed ranks of our own notable men or from Japanese-trained company men, the factories cannot function without able technicians and experienced administrators to run them. Let it be known that Xinan is a land of opportunity and cheap labor for those who would lay hold of it.
strings.YUN_a_united_southwest_desc: Just as Yunnan was ordered under Lu Han and his chosen few, so too shall Guizhou be incorporated into the new state. With one vision we have unified the Southwest and none shall come between the people of the Southwest again. It is important that we make sure the people themselves understand that fact.
strings.YUN_biased_land_distribution_desc: He Yingqin himself held not inconsiderable land, and the same can be said of many of his old allies. Their lands now lay open, with their laborers anxious to learn what will become of them. Naturally those close to Lu Han as well as those who have been so instrumental in the creation of Xinan ought to be given first pick of the unowned land, and a simple vetted auction will quite easily take... some of this land off of Lu's hands. Some shall be acquired by Lu Han himself, naturally.
strings.YUN_two_brothers_still_desc: While the names have been changed and the borders have been redrawn, the simple fact remains that Yunnan and Guizhou are not the same land and cannot be treated as such. Under the watchful eye of Lu Han only the highest level of administration shall be fully changed, and local life may go on much as it has before the merging of the two. The boss's boss may change and the taxes are paid to a different man, but it is best not to offend unnecessarily.
strings.YUN_rational_infrastructure_desc: Perhaps the greatest enemy of wealth in Xinan is its poor infrastructure. Winding through mountains the roads often lead to nowhere, or to towns long since declined after the war. As the ruler of two provinces it is finally possible to rationalize and connect the infrastructure of both, with all the benefits which accompany such endeavors.
strings.YUN_let_the_work_begin_desc: Order has finally been restored to the lands of Xinan. United and whole the investment of both money and talent has started to accumulate in the cities and in the fields. We have achieved recognition the world over. In this new era of stability economic progress shall continue on without end, and the families closest to Lu Han shall be at the forefront of it. Let the new work begin!
strings.YUN_playing_to_our_strengths_desc:
The great state of Xinan has been undervalued by the establishment in Nanjing and Tokyo. Our fields and forests grow thick with produce. Our mines are deep and well-dug. Our peasants work as hard and for as little pay as any peasant in the whole Sphere.

But there is room here for improvement. Our fields are great but still too small, too ancient in their design. Our mines could be dug so much deeper, so much more greedily, and our peasants often have enough time in the day to partake in indolence, and they would not suffer much to be a little hungrier.

We understand that this is not the conventional wisdom. The Reorganized Government seeks to move beyond being a 'mere' breadbasket, This suits us in two ways. First of all the demand for raw materials grows ever stronger as new factories flicker into life, and second of all the stomach of the sphere will grow no less hungry as the cities rise and sprawl from the dirt like the wild mushrooms we export in great, yet inadequate quantities.

We will seize the mantle as the true 'breadbasket' of the Sphere, and Xinan will provide the raw firmament they shall twist into the miracles of a new age.
strings.YUN_survey_the_land_desc:
Many of our mines have been in operation for hundreds of years. This isn't an issue on its own, but it reveals a shocking lack of progress in this, the cornerstone of our economy. Our landscape is draped in mountains and plateaus, the buried bounty of the Earth lies just beyond our grasp. But not for long. We must bring our eyes to bare upon these resources, opening bold new avenues of tin, lead, zinc, iron, silver, gold and coal, as well as a hundred other roads that we shall take to prosperity.

For this task the few experts we have to hand will be rallied, along with a few experts in geology, geography, metallurgy, and the mining industry from as far away as Manchuria. The likely candidates first, near existing mines. After these have been examined we shall move on to new pastures that we shall rip up and exploit. Once we have the facilities in place, all gathered under a new 'Bureau of Expansion, Efficiency, and Exploitation', we shall methodically and thoroughly examine the country for likely sites. The land must be numbered, weighed for its potential and divided into new zones for development.

Some of these developments will be resisted by reactionary elements who fear progress. They will protest that we would destroy their villages, their forests and their fields. But the march of time is inexorable, We have not yet begun the survey, but the writing is on the wall.
strings.YUN_survey_the_land_tt: Unlocks decisions to survey the states of {yun_getflag} {yun_getname} for resources.
strings.YUN_open_new_mines_desc:
More than 500 metres of ribbon, at least, is required for the hundreds of opening ceremonies we have planned for the next few months. If local stocks are inadequate, we have agents in our neighbours seeking emergency ribbon suppliers. A junior member of the Bureau of Expansion, Efficiency, and Exploitation has suggested we delay the opening ceremonies of certain mines to save on expenses.

After firing him we have come slightly closer to a great leap forward, towards full exploitation of our natural resources. This is a tremendous moment for dozens of communities around Xinan who will soon have access to exciting new jobs in our mineshafts. Some villages in the end did have to be relocated, but their employment in making Xinan the master of metals is an opportunity we are sure they would thank us for if we ever ask them.

Having said that, a debate still rages in Kunming over the precise colour and type of ribbon to be used. Not a single mine can be opened until this is settled!
strings.YUN_open_new_mines_tt: Unlocks decisions to mine the minerals of previously surveyed states.
strings.YUN_japanese_equipment_desc:
It's not our peasants fault that their frail bodies and lazy souls are inadequate for our needs. It is their fault that their home-made tools keep breaking when put under the necessary stresses of a modern mining environment. Even the tools made by our small manufacturing base prove inadequate. No one in Xinan thinks big enough to make the tools we need!

For this reason we must look further afield for our tools. The mines of the Reorganized Government and Manchuria are both seeking to modernise, meaning that much of their old equipment is going to be for sale. We will be a welcome market for these cast-offs, but more excitingly a number of Japanese manufacturers have took notice of our efforts, and have contacted us offering to sell the latest in drilling, extracting, and processing technology.
